documents.keywords: How many of the new homes completed in 2026 the PBO expects to get the first-time buyers’ rebate A projection made in June 2025, not a count of claims. Of 237,324 homes projected to be completed in 2026, the PBO expects 12,903 (5.4%) to receive the rebate. The largest cuts are homes built for rent and homes not bought as a primary residence (investors, non-residents, temporary residents and corporations cannot claim), then the step to first-time buyers: about 20% of qualifying sales in the PBO’s Canadian Housing Statistics Program data for three provinces. Over 2025 to 2030 it projects 71,711 rebates averaging $26,832, costing about CAD 1.9 billion. The PBO assumed agreements after 26 May 2025; the law as enacted reaches back to 20 March 2025.

documents.description: 价格不超过 100 万加元时，首次置业人士无须缴付联邦 GST：两项回扣合共退还全部税款，最多 50,000 加元。由 100 万加元起，回扣以直线递减至 150 万加元时的零，而税款持续上升，所以应缴 GST 在这 500,000 加元内由 0 加元升至 75,000 加元。其他自住买家最多只得 6,300 加元，价格达 450,000 加元或以上则一分也没有。您的价格 $1,100,000：回扣 $40,000，应缴 GST $15,000。

documents.keywords: Federal GST (or federal part of the HST), the rebates and the tax still payable, by price of the new home Up to CAD 1 million a first-time buyer pays no federal GST: the two rebates together return all of it, and CAD 50,000 is the most. From CAD 1 million the rebate falls in a straight line to nil at CAD 1.5 million, while the tax keeps rising, so the GST payable climbs from CAD 0 to CAD 75,000 over that CAD 500,000. Any other buyer of a home they will live in gets at most CAD 6,300, and nothing at CAD 450,000 or more. Your price, $1,100,000: rebates $40,000, GST payable $15,000.

documents.parentTitle: 首次置业人士新屋 GST 回扣：最多退还 50,000 加元、100 万至 150 万加元之间的 15% 边际税，以及升级的真正成本
documents.description: 这是仍须缴付 GST 的斜率。在递减区间内，价格每多一元，税项增加 5 仙，回扣减少 10 仙（在 500,000 加元内减少 50,000 加元），因此首次置业人士在 100 万至 150 万加元之间的边际税率为 15%，是法定 5% 的三倍。其他买家在 350,000 加元以下面对 3.2%（5% 减去 36% 回扣），在 350,000 至 450,000 加元之间面对 11.3%（5% 加上在 100,000 加元内失去的 6,300 加元）。超过各区间上限后，税率回到 5%。升级、更大的单位和价格调整都按这些税率计税。

documents.keywords: Federal sales tax on the next dollar of price: first-time buyer and other buyers The slope of the GST still payable. Inside the phase-out, each extra dollar of price adds 5 cents of tax and removes 10 cents of rebate (CAD 50,000 over CAD 500,000), so the first-time buyer’s marginal rate is 15% between CAD 1 million and 1.5 million, three times the statutory 5%. Other buyers face 3.2% below CAD 350,000 (5% less the 36% rebate) and 11.3% between CAD 350,000 and 450,000 (5% plus CAD 6,300 lost over CAD 100,000). Above the top of each band, the rate returns to 5%. Upgrades, a bigger unit and price escalations are all taxed at these rates.

documents.title: 加入 $50,000 对首次置业人士的成本，按起始价格
documents.parentTitle: 首次置业人士新屋 GST 回扣：最多退还 50,000 加元、100 万至 150 万加元之间的 15% 边际税，以及升级的真正成本
documents.description: 每一对柱都是在不同起始价格上加入同样的 $50,000，适用于合资格的买家。低于 100 万加元时，只要总价仍低于 100 万加元，增加的部分不会产生 GST；一旦总价超过 100 万加元，超过部分每元带来 15 仙；由 150 万加元起，回落至 5 仙。计算器把向建筑商购买的升级视为协议价格的一部分，因此一张更改单可能令价格越过门槛；请向建筑商确认总代价。成交后向其他人购买的工程，属另一项购买。
documents.body: Each pair is the same $50,000 added at a different starting price, for a buyer who qualifies. Below CAD 1 million the addition costs no GST if the total stays under CAD 1 million; once the total crosses it, each dollar above CAD 1 million carries 15 cents; from CAD 1.5 million it is back to 5 cents. The calculator treats upgrades bought from the builder as part of the price on the agreement, so a change order can cross a threshold; confirm the total consideration with the builder. Work bought from someone else after closing is a separate purchase.

documents.title: FHSA 超额供款：每月最高超额的 1% 税、指定提款能修正和不能修正什么，以及超额如何蚕食下一年的额度
documents.description: 按月追踪《所得税法》的 FHSA 超额：为何没有缓冲、为何移除超额后当月仍要缴税、为何指定提款无法预先抵销薪金供款、应税提款如何产生重新参与额度，以及 12 月留下的超额如何减少下一年 1 月的额度。使用 CRA 2024 年 FHSA 统计数据。
documents.body: A first home savings account (FHSA) has no over-contribution cushion. Any contributions and RRSP transfers above your participation room, across all your FHSAs, are an excess FHSA amount, taxed at 1% of the highest excess at any time in each month. Withdrawing it stops the tax from the next month, not the current one. A designated withdrawal (Form RC727) is tax-free but limited to the excess at that moment, so it cannot get ahead of payroll contributions that are still coming. An excess left at year-end is absorbed by the next January’s room, which leaves less room for that year. In 2024 FHSA holders had 225,210 more accounts than people. How an FHSA excess starts The first home savings account (FHSA) gives each eligible first-time buyer CAD 8,000 of participation room a year, up to CAD 40,000 in a lifetime, with up to CAD 8,000 of unused room carried into the next year. The room belongs to the person , not the account. Most excesses come from that detail: a payroll plan at one institution keeps contributing after a lump sum or an RRSP transfer has gone into an FHSA at another; carried-forward room is counted twice; or a holder assumes that a withdrawal gives room back, as it does for a TFSA the following year. The calculator follows a single person through 2026 and 2027 with a monthly contribution, one lump sum or RRSP transfer, one withdrawal and the new room that arrives on 1 January 2027. It answers four questions: when does the excess start, how much does a withdrawal save and in which month, which kind of withdrawal to use, and how much room is left for next year. The excess FHSA amount and its tax, in the Act’s terms Section 207.01(1) of the Income Tax Act defines the excess FHSA amount at any time in a year as A + B + C − D − E − F: Section 207.021 then charges, for each month in which there is an excess at any time, 1% of the highest such amount in that month . Three consequences follow: No cushion. An RRSP allows CAD 2,000 over the limit before tax applies; an FHSA allows nothing. The first dollar over room is taxed. The month of the fix is still taxed. The test is the highest amount at any time in the month, as for a TFSA. Removing the excess on the 28th still leaves that month’s 1%; it stops the tax from the next month. Under the RRSP rule, which uses the month-end, the same withdrawal would avoid the month. The excess does not lapse. It carries into the next year as element A and is absorbed only by that year’s new room or by a withdrawal. Five worked cases All use the calculator’s default: an FHSA opened in 2025 with CAD 3,000 contributed, which gives CAD 13,000 of room for 2026 (CAD 8,000 plus CAD 5,000 carried forward); CAD 500 a month by payroll at one institution through 2026; CAD 10,000 put into a second FHSA at another institution in April; and CAD 500 a month in 2027. Contributions reach CAD 13,000 in June and the excess starts in July. Nothing withdrawn. The highest excess is CAD 500 in July, rising by CAD 500 a month to CAD 3,000 in December: 1% of the total CAD 10,500 is CAD 105 for 2026. On 1 January 2027 the CAD 3,000 still over is absorbed by the CAD 8,000 of new room, leaving CAD 5,000; at CAD 500 a month that runs out in October 2027, and November and December cost another CAD 15 . Total CAD 120. CAD 2,000 designated and withdrawn in October (the default). October is still taxed on its CAD 2,000 high point, and payroll rebuilds CAD 500 and CAD 1,000 in November and December: CAD 65 for 2026. The CAD 1,000 left in December uses part of 2027’s new room, leaving CAD 7,000, and 2027 stays within it. The best single month. Designating the whole excess in July, August, September, October, November or December gives CAD 85, 65, 60, 65, 80 and 105. Early withdrawals are small because the excess is small, and payroll recreates it; late ones come after months of tax. September is the cheapest here, but stopping the payroll contributions in July would beat every one of them. A taxable withdrawal of CAD 5,000 in October. The first CAD 2,000 reduces the excess, so the excess tax is the same CAD 65. The full CAD 5,000 is income, about CAD 1,500 at a 30% marginal rate, and the CAD 3,000 above the excess becomes re-participation room: 2027 room is CAD 10,000 after the CAD 1,000 carried in. CRA’s own examples. With the inputs set to them, the calculator reproduces the five checked cases on CRA’s pages: CAD 10,000 contributed in November against CAD 8,000 of room costs CAD 40 and leaves CAD 6,000 of room the next year; CAD 13,000 leaves CAD 3,000; a CAD 5,000 taxable withdrawal of a CAD 2,000 excess leaves CAD 11,000; a CAD 7,500 taxable withdrawal of a CAD 6,000 excess leaves CAD 9,500; and a CAD 1,500 excess removed the next month costs two months, CAD 30. Designated or taxable: two ways out CRA’s excess FHSA amounts page lists the ways an excess is reduced: new participation room on 1 January, a designated withdrawal, a designated transfer to an RRSP or RRIF, a taxable withdrawal, or income deemed received when the FHSA ceases. If the excess came from an RRSP transfer, a designated transfer back to an RRSP or RRIF is the counterpart of a designated withdrawal; it is not income and does not affect RRSP deduction room. Someone who only contributed can only make a designated withdrawal, and someone who only transferred can only make a designated transfer. The calculator treats contributions and transfers alike and models the withdrawal route. Because the designated amount cannot exceed the excess when it is designated, it is a correction, not a reserve. The contributions that are still scheduled have to be stopped or reduced, or the excess comes back the next month, as the third chart shows. What 1 January does, and what it costs CRA says an excess is reduced or eliminated by your new participation room on 1 January of the following year. That ends the tax without a withdrawal, but it is not free: The excess uses next year’s room. CRA’s example of a CAD 2,000 excess at the end of 2025 leaves CAD 6,000 of room for 2026, not CAD 8,000. No carryforward is created. A year that ends over room has no unused room to carry forward, so the next year’s room is CAD 8,000 at most before the excess is subtracted. The lifetime limit still counts the money. Contributions above room count against the CAD 40,000 until they are designated out. Months of 1% tax run first. In the default case, waiting costs CAD 120 over two years against CAD 65 for a designated withdrawal in October. CRA’s participation room page distinguishes the participation room carryforward , used for room and excess calculations, from the FHSA carryforward in section 146.6(1) , used for the annual FHSA limit and deductions. They are equal in simple cases like these. What CRA’s 2024 statistics show CRA’s First Home Savings Account Statistics for the 2024 tax year, built from T4FHSA slips filed by financial institutions and processed to 30 June 2026, count 1,455,280 holders with 1,680,490 accounts: 1.155 accounts per holder . Room is shared across a person’s FHSAs, so each extra account is another place a contribution can be made without the first institution knowing. Averages are total contributions divided by holders who contributed; CRA rounds counts to the nearest 10 and dollars to the nearest thousand. 2024 was the second year of the FHSA, the first in which carried-forward room let a holder put in more than CAD 8,000, and the two highest brackets averaged above it. Statistics Canada’s table for 2023 , the first year, reports 484,320 contributors with a median of exactly CAD 8,000: many people contribute at the limit, where one extra deposit is an excess. Neither source counts excess amounts, so these figures describe exposure, not the number of people taxed. If you are already over Add up every FHSA. Room is per person, so list contributions and transfers at every institution against the room on your notice of assessment or CRA account. Stop or reduce scheduled contributions until 1 January, or the excess returns. Ask each issuer for a designated withdrawal (or a designated transfer, if the excess came from an RRSP) on Form RC727, for no more than the excess at the time. Do it as early in a month as you can: the current month is taxed either way, and every further month adds 1%. File Form RC728 with Schedule A and pay by 30 June of the following year: by 30 June 2027 for an excess in 2026. CRA’s FHSA taxes page says a penalty and interest apply if you file late. Ask for a waiver if it was a reasonable error. CRA’s form for this tax is RC729 , Request for Waiver or Cancellation of Tax on your Excess FHSA Amount, sent with FHSA statements showing when the excess arose and when it was removed. Penalties and interest go through Form RC4288 instead. What the calculator leaves out Growth. Amounts are contributions, not market values. Investment income does not use room, so an account worth more than you put in does not by itself show an excess. The 2026 room is entered, not derived. Enter it after any carryforward and re-participation room, within the lifetime limit; the 2027 room is calculated from it with the rules above. One withdrawal, made after that month’s contributions. Several withdrawals, designated transfers to an RRSP or RRIF, and qualifying withdrawals for a home are not modelled. Income tax is a flat estimate. A taxable withdrawal is priced at your entered marginal rate; withholding at source and the effect on benefits are not shown. Eligibility and deadlines. The maximum participation period, account closure and the year after a first qualifying withdrawal end the ability to contribute and are not checked. Penalties and interest on a late RC728 are not included.
documents.keywords: FHSA over-contribution: the 1% tax on the highest excess each month, what a designated withdrawal can and cannot fix, and how the excess eats next year’s room Follow the Income Tax Act’s excess FHSA amount month by month: why there is no cushion, why removing the excess still leaves that month taxed, why a designated withdrawal cannot get ahead of payroll contributions, how a taxable withdrawal creates re-participation room, and how an excess left in December reduces the next January’s room. Uses CRA’s FHSA statistics for 2024.

documents.keywords: Average FHSA contribution per contributing holder in 2024, by federal tax bracket, beside the CAD 8,000 annual limit In 2024, 1.04 million of 1.46 million FHSA holders contributed a total of CAD 6.47 billion, an average of $6,231. In the two highest brackets the average was above CAD 8,000, which is possible only with carried-forward room. Holders had 1,680,490 accounts, 225,210 more than holders; room is shared across all of a person’s FHSAs, which is how many excesses start. Averages are total contributions divided by contributors (CRA rounds counts to 10 and dollars to the thousand); they are not medians. CRA does not publish how many holders had an excess, so this chart shows the people exposed, not the number taxed.

documents.title: 超出参与额度的供款，以及每月须缴税的最高超额，2026 至 2027 年

documents.description: 低于零代表仍未使用的额度。没有缓冲：超出额度的第一元就是超额。在有提款的月份，最高超额是提款前的金额，所以两条线会分开。2027 年 1 月有 $8,000 新额度到来（8,000 加元加任何结转额度和重新参与额度，并在 40,000 加元终身上限之内），再减去结转的 $1,000 超额。

documents.keywords: Contributions over your participation room, and the highest excess taxed in each month, 2026 to 2027 Below zero is room still unused. There is no cushion: the first dollar over room is an excess. In a month with a withdrawal, the highest excess is the amount before it, so the two lines part. In January 2027 new room of $8,000 arrives (CAD 8,000 plus any carryforward and re-participation room, within the CAD 40,000 lifetime limit), minus the $1,000 excess carried in.

documents.keywords: Total tax if all of the excess present is designated and withdrawn in one month Each bar removes the whole excess in that month and changes nothing else. A designated withdrawal cannot exceed the excess when it is made, so it cannot get ahead of contributions that are still coming. If payroll contributions continue, a new excess appears the next month; stopping them matters as much as the withdrawal. The month of the withdrawal is still taxed, because the tax uses the highest excess at any time in the month.

documents.title: 处理超额的三种方法：2026 年 10 月取出 $2,000，或等待 1 月
documents.parentTitle: FHSA 超额供款：每月最高超额的 1% 税、指定提款能修正和不能修正什么，以及超额如何蚕食下一年的额度
documents.description: 指定提款以当时的超额为限（这里是 $2,000），不计入收入，并恢复同等金额的 40,000 加元终身上限。应税提款也会减少超额，但全部金额都计入收入；超出超额的部分在下一年成为重新参与额度，而不是终身额度。等待则让 1 月 1 日吸收超额，代价是几个月的税和较少的新额度。所得税是按金额以固定 30% 估算，并非报税计算。

documents.keywords: Three ways to deal with the excess: $2,000 in October 2026, or waiting for January A designated withdrawal is limited to the excess at the time (here $2,000), is not income, and restores that much of the CAD 40,000 lifetime limit. A taxable withdrawal reduces the excess too, but the whole amount is income; any part above the excess becomes re-participation room the next year rather than lifetime room. Waiting lets 1 January absorb the excess, at the cost of months of tax and less new room. Income tax is a flat 30% estimate on the amount, not a return calculation.

documents.title: 哪只基金应该放进 TFSA？比较把债券基金或股票基金放进有限的免税额度
documents.description: 在 TFSA 和非注册账户中持有相同的债券基金和股票基金，只改变哪只基金放在哪里。比较不同回报假设下每年收入的税款、最终出售时的税款以及税后结果。
documents.body: The TFSA, not the fund, provides the tax shelter. Sheltering a bond fund avoids yearly tax on interest; sheltering an equity fund lets a higher but uncertain return compound without tax. Which helps more depends on the returns, the tax rates and the holding period, so test the placement rather than assume it. The account sets the tax rules; the fund sets the income it produces A mutual fund or ETF is not tax-exempt by itself. Inside a TFSA, CRA says income such as interest, dividends or capital gains is generally tax-free, even when you withdraw. The same fund held in a non-registered account is taxed under the ordinary rules: CRA’s guidance on mutual funds explains that interest, dividends and capital gains distributed by a fund are reported in the year they are paid, even when the distribution is reinvested in more units. Many investors hold more than one fund and more than one account. If TFSA room is limited, a practical question follows: which fund should use the tax-free space first? This is often called asset location. It is a different decision from asset allocation. The combined mix, here 40% bond fund and 60% equity fund, stays the same in every comparison; only the account holding each fund changes. TFSA room arrives a few thousand dollars at a time The first chart shows CRA’s TFSA dollar limits. The limit was CAD 5,000 in 2009, CAD 10,000 in 2015, and has been CAD 7,000 for each of 2024, 2025 and 2026 . The limits for 2009 to 2026 add up to CAD 109,000. That total applies only to someone who was 18 or older and resident in Canada since 2009 and has never contributed; your own room depends on your age, residency, contributions and withdrawals, and CRA’s My Account shows it. Room is usually filled in one of two ways. A person may contribute part of each paycheque as it is earned, or move an existing lump sum, perhaps a non-registered holding, into the TFSA. Moving existing units in kind counts as a contribution at market value and can realize a gain in the non-registered account, as the in-kind contribution guide shows. Either way, the room is finite, so what goes into it matters. How the comparison taxes each fund The model starts with CAD 40,000 in a TFSA and CAD 60,000 in a non-registered account. The bond fund returns 4% a year, all paid as interest. The equity fund grows 5% a year in price and also distributes 2% a year, which is reinvested. In the non-registered account: bond interest is taxed every year at the entered marginal rate, 30% by default; equity distributions are taxed every year at a separate entered rate, 15% by default, as a simple stand-in for a mix of dividends and capital gains distributions; reinvested after-tax distributions raise the adjusted cost base, as CRA’s mutual-fund guidance describes; unrealized price growth is taxed only when the units are sold, at the marginal rate times the one-half inclusion rate shown in CRA’s capital gains guidance. Three placements are compared. Bond first puts all CAD 40,000 of bond fund in the TFSA and holds the equity fund outside. Equity first puts CAD 40,000 of equity fund in the TFSA and leaves the bond fund and the remaining equity outside. Same mix holds 40/60 in each account. Fund fees are assumed to be included in the entered returns. Under the defaults, the gap is small and changes sign over time After 20 years and a sale of the non-registered holdings, bond first ends at about CAD 289,293 after tax, the same mix at about CAD 290,613 and equity first at about CAD 291,493 . The difference between the extremes is about CAD 2,201 on a starting CAD 100,000, roughly 0.8% of the ending value. The tax pattern differs much more than the result. Bond first pays about CAD 7,142 of tax on yearly income over the 20 years but leaves about CAD 17,855 of tax due on the final equity sale. Equity first pays about CAD 15,019 on yearly income, mostly interest, and only about CAD 5,952 on the sale. Deferral and the half inclusion rate make unrealized equity growth relatively tax-efficient outside the TFSA; interest has neither advantage. The difference chart shows the timing. Equity first trails by about CAD 247 at year five and CAD 223 at year ten, then moves ahead: CAD 408 at year 15 and CAD 2,201 at year 20. Over a short holding period, sheltering the interest won; over a longer one, sheltering the faster-growing fund won. A different set of inputs can reverse both. The answer depends on the gap between expected returns The grid reruns the 20-year comparison while changing only the equity fund’s price growth and the bond fund’s return. With equity growth of 2% (4% total return including distributions) and a 4% bond fund, bond first is ahead by about CAD 9,771. With equity growth of 8% and a 6% bond fund, equity first is ahead by about CAD 3,669. When bonds pay more relative to equities, the yearly tax on interest weighs more; when equities are expected to earn much more, tax-free compounding of that return weighs more. Expected returns are uncertain. An equity fund’s higher average return comes with larger losses in some years, and no allocation guarantees the higher return arrives during your holding period. A placement chosen on an optimistic equity assumption can still be the wrong one if returns disappoint. Placement also changes where gains and losses land Equity first puts the more volatile fund in the TFSA. After a market fall, the TFSA balance drops more than in the bond-first layout. A loss inside a TFSA cannot be claimed as a capital loss, and the lower value does not create new contribution room; the TFSA loss guide traces that effect. Outside registered plans, CRA allows capital losses to offset capital gains, with any net capital loss carried back three years or forward indefinitely, though not against other income. The model gives a loss on sale no tax value, which understates the non-registered account’s flexibility. The placements also differ in after-tax risk. The government shares part of the gains and, through loss offsets, part of the losses in a taxable account, but nothing in a TFSA. Two portfolios with the same pre-tax 40/60 mix can therefore carry different after-tax exposure. That is one reason to treat asset location as a refinement after the allocation is right, not a replacement for it. A checklist before you move funds between accounts Choose the overall mix first, for example a balanced fund or a bond/equity split you can hold through a decline. List each fund’s typical income: interest, dividends, capital gains distributions and return of capital. Fund Facts and annual tax slips show the history; past distributions are not guaranteed. Compare the yearly tax on that income in a non-registered account with the tax deferred on unrealized gains. Consider an RRSP separately. Income grows without current tax there, but withdrawals are generally taxed as ordinary income, so the lower tax on capital gains and dividends does not carry through; see the RRSP and TFSA timing guide . Before selling a non-registered holding to rearrange accounts, estimate the capital gain the sale realizes. The fund-switch break-even guide tests whether a lower fee or better location repays that tax. Keep cash for reinvested distributions. A distribution reinvested outside a TFSA is still taxable; the distribution provision guide plans for it. A single balanced fund held in both accounts, the “same mix” bar, gives up a little potential optimization in exchange for simplicity and an identical risk profile in each account. For many households that trade-off is reasonable. Provincial tax, foreign withholding tax on foreign dividends, dividend gross-up and credit details, and personal circumstances can all change the result; a tax professional can review the specifics.
documents.keywords: Which fund belongs in the TFSA? Compare placing a bond fund or an equity fund in limited tax-free room Hold the same bond fund and equity fund in a TFSA and a non-registered account, then change only which fund sits where. Compare yearly tax on income, tax on the final sale and the after-tax result across return assumptions.

documents.title: 错过最好的月份、避开最差的月份：为什么两种统计都会误导，以及真实的离场会怎样
documents.description: 从一段自拟的十年中剔除最强的月份、最弱的月份或两者，然后测试一条真实的规则：在某个月末收盘后离场，之后再回来。看看为什么大涨和大跌往往同时出现。
documents.body: “Missing the best days” and “avoiding the worst days” are hindsight exercises. In volatile stretches the best and worst periods sit side by side, so an exit usually skips some of each. Whether an exit helps depends on dates nobody knows in advance, which is why a written allocation usually serves crash worry better than a forecast. Two famous statistics, and the question neither one answers Investment articles often show that an investor who missed a handful of the market’s best days ended with far less money than one who stayed invested. A reply soon follows: an investor who missed the worst days would have done far better. Both calculations are correct and both are hindsight. Nobody can list the best or worst periods before they happen. The useful question is what happens to someone who follows a rule they could actually follow, such as “move to cash after this month-end and come back in six months.” This guide answers both with one authored ten-year path for an existing CAD 10,000 balance. The path is deliberately simple: calm months averaging about 0.5%, a 14-month crisis in months 41 to 54 in which large losses and large gains alternate, then a recovery. Any month spent out of the market earns cash interest, 2.25% a year by default. Remove the best months, the worst months, or both Fully invested, CAD 10,000 grows to about CAD 18,045 . Remove the five best months and it ends at about CAD 12,740 . Remove the five worst months and it ends at about CAD 27,590 . Remove both sets and it ends at about CAD 19,479 , close to staying invested. The count chart extends this from zero to ten months. Missing more best months keeps lowering the result; missing more worst months keeps raising it. The line for missing both stays within a few thousand dollars of the fully invested balance. Missing both is a closer description of what an imperfect exit does, because of where the months fall. A practical note: removing a fixed set of months gives the same ending value whatever order the months occur in. Order matters only once a person must choose an exit date, and that is where clustering becomes decisive. The best months are found next to the worst months In this path the five best months are months 45, 47, 48, 50 and 52; the five worst are 41, 43, 44, 46 and 49. Each best month sits on average about 1.4 months from the nearest worst month. The clustering chart lists them in calendar order. That arrangement is authored, but it reflects an observation regulators make about real markets. FINRA notes that some of the top trading days occur during periods of greater volatility, so an investor who sells during a sharp but temporary decline may miss the rebound. The months that test nerves and the months that reward patience tend to arrive together. A rule you could follow: leave after a month-end and return later The default exit leaves after the close of month 46, just after the deepest monthly loss, when fear is likely to be greatest, and stays out for six months. The window skips four strong months and two weak ones. The balance ends at about CAD 15,157 , about CAD 2,888 below staying invested. The heatmap shows fifteen windows. Leaving after month 40, before the trouble starts, and staying out for six months ends about CAD 5,043 ahead, because the window happens to skip the first crash months. Leaving after month 46 for twelve months ends about CAD 4,224 behind. The best cells require knowing that a crisis is about to start; the worst cells follow the natural reaction of selling after large losses and waiting for calm. Choosing the dates required the whole path, which no investor has. Leaving is also only half of the decision. The exit and re-entry guide shows that the rule for coming back can matter as much as the rule for leaving. Selling a fund in a non-registered account is also a disposition for tax purposes, which this model does not charge. New pay is a separate decision from an existing balance This guide follows a balance already invested. Money arriving from each paycheque raises a different question: whether to keep investing it on schedule during a volatile period. Regular contributions keep buying through a window like the one above, including some of the low-priced months. Holding new pay in cash until conditions look better turns each deposit into a timing decision; the dip-waiting guide tests that rule, and the cash-floor guide checks whether contributions remain affordable if income stops. Responding to crash worry without forecasting the crash Worry about a financial-crisis-style fall is reasonable, especially for money needed within a few years. The Ontario Securities Commission’s investor education site suggests staying with a diversified portfolio that fits your plan and warns that trying to time the market can mean losses when prices drop and missed gains when they recover. Those points suggest acting on the allocation rather than the calendar: Keep money needed in the next few years outside equities, in cash or short-term savings sized to the expense. Choose an equity share whose loss in a crisis you could hold through; a balanced fund or a mix with bonds lowers the size of a fall but does not prevent one. Write a rebalancing rule in advance; the rebalancing guide shows how one behaves through a crash. Check the costs and tax of any sale before trading in a non-registered account. If a decline would force a change in plans, the risk is too high for the goal, whatever the market does next. None of these steps promises a recovery by a particular date. Markets have recovered from past declines, but recoveries have taken different lengths of time, and a diversified portfolio can still lose value for years.
documents.keywords: Missing the best months, avoiding the worst: why both statistics mislead, and what an actual exit does Remove the strongest months, the weakest months, or both from an authored decade, then test a real rule: leave after a month-end close and return later. See why large gains and losses tend to arrive together.

documents.description: 按时间顺序列出。在这条路径中，每个最好的月份平均距离最近的最差月份 1.4 个月。避开某个最差月份的离场，很可能也会错过某个最好的月份，因为两者都出现在同一段波动期间。
documents.body: 按时间顺序列出。在这条路径中，每个最好的月份平均距离最近的最差月份 1.4 个月。避开某个最差月份的离场，很可能也会错过某个最好的月份，因为两者都出现在同一段波动期间。
documents.keywords: The strongest and weakest months sit next to each other Listed in calendar order. On average, each best month is 1.4 months from the nearest worst month in this path. An exit that avoids one of the worst months is likely to be out for one of the best, because both arrive during the same volatile stretch.

documents.title: 错过最好的月份、最差的月份或两者，按剔除数量比较
documents.parentTitle: 错过最好的月份、避开最差的月份：为什么两种统计都会误导，以及真实的离场会怎样
documents.description: 只剔除最好的月份是常见的警告；只剔除最差的月份是常见的诱惑。两者都依赖完美的事后判断。“两者”这条线更接近收益和亏损聚集时不完美离场的效果：两种月份都会错过一些。
documents.body: 只剔除最好的月份是常见的警告；只剔除最差的月份是常见的诱惑。两者都依赖完美的事后判断。“两者”这条线更接近收益和亏损聚集时不完美离场的效果：两种月份都会错过一些。
documents.keywords: Missing best months, worst months, or both, by how many are removed Removing only the best months is the familiar warning; removing only the worst is the familiar temptation. Both use perfect hindsight. The “both” line is closer to what an imperfect exit tends to do when gains and losses cluster: it misses some of each.

documents.keywords: A real exit window: ending value minus staying invested Each cell leaves after the stated month-end close and returns after the stated number of months, earning the entered cash rate while out. Positive cells beat staying invested in this one authored path; negative cells trail it. The result depends on the exact dates, which were chosen here with the whole path in view.

documents.title: 等待回调再投入每期工资：用定期买入检验这条规则
documents.description: 把每月新增储蓄留作现金，直到市场下跌一定幅度再买入，或在每笔存款到账时直接投资。在三条设定路径上比较现金排队、买入价格和期末价值。
documents.body: A buy-the-dip rule for new pay turns every paycheque into a timing decision. Cash can earn interest while it waits, but the rule can miss a rise, buy after a late dip at a higher price than earlier months, or never fire at all. Write the waiting limit before the first deposit. The question is about new money, not an existing lump sum Many regular savers invest each deposit soon after their pay arrives. A common alternative is to hold new savings in cash and invest only after prices fall: “I will buy when the market is 10% below its high.” This guide tests that rule for money that arrives monthly from earnings. That is a different decision from staging a lump sum already on hand. With a lump sum, phased purchases leave part of an existing balance in cash by design; the lump-sum comparison covers that case. FINRA notes that the cash-drag concern applies mainly when a pool of cash is waiting, and that contributions invested as they are earned do not sit idle. A dip rule recreates a cash pool out of new pay. The model gives both rules the same deposit at each of 36 month-ends. The regular rule buys at that month’s close. The waiting rule holds the deposit in cash, earns the entered interest rate, and buys everything waiting at the first close that is at least the trigger percentage below the highest close observed so far, or once the oldest waiting deposit reaches the entered waiting limit. Waiting cash earns a rate, and prices keep moving too The first chart places two dated public figures side by side. Statistics Canada reported that all-items CPI rose 3.1% year over year in September 2026 . The Bank of Canada’s target for the overnight rate was 2.25% on 22 October 2026 . A deposit account, GIC or money market fund can pay a different rate, and neither figure says what inflation or interest will be while your cash waits. The scenario uses a separate cash rate, set by default to 2.25% as an illustration. Interest earned outside a registered account is generally taxable; tax is not deducted in the model. Inside a TFSA, CRA says income earned is generally tax-free, but a deposit still uses contribution room whether the money stays in cash or buys a fund. The account sets the tax rules; the investment inside it still carries its own risk, fees and liquidity terms. A trigger based on the running peak can fire late, or not at all The index chart shows the authored index and the trigger line, which follows the running peak. Because the peak keeps rising in a long advance, a dip can begin well above prices that regular purchases already paid. In the default early dip, then recovery path, the 10% trigger first fires at month five. Waiting cash is then invested through month ten while the index stays below the line. After the recovery, new deposits wait again until the 12-month limit forces purchases at months 23 and 36. Under these defaults, the regular rule ends at about CAD 21,127 and the waiting rule at about CAD 20,760 , including interest on waiting cash. The waiting rule’s average cost per unit is about 103.93 index points, versus 101.25 for investing every month. It caught a dip but paid more on average because later deposits waited through the rise. The path comparison shows why one example settles nothing. On the steady rise path the 10% trigger never fires, so purchases happen only when the waiting limit forces them; the regular rule ends ahead, CAD 19,214 versus CAD 19,003. On the long rise, late dip path the waiting rule ends ahead, CAD 18,826 versus CAD 18,603. Neither result is a probability or a backtest. The waiting limit is the rule’s most important setting Set the waiting limit to zero and the waiting rule becomes regular investing: each deposit is bought at the close on which it arrives. Raise the limit and the rule can hold more money in cash for longer. If the trigger never arrives, the cash queue can keep growing, and so can the gap if prices rise. FINRA’s market-timing guidance warns that short-term price moves are difficult to predict and that some of the strongest market days can occur during volatile periods. A rule written in advance avoids changing the threshold after seeing prices, but it does not make the decision free. Before using a dip trigger, decide: the exact trigger and the price series it uses; the longest time any deposit may wait; where waiting cash is held, what it earns and how it is taxed; whether purchases have commissions, spreads or fund minimums; whether the investment’s risk still suits the goal if the dip deepens after you buy. If the worry is a crash, adjust the mix instead of the calendar Concern about a large decline is reasonable, especially near a spending date. Holding every new deposit until a dip mixes two decisions: how much risk the portfolio should carry and when to buy it. Often the clearer adjustment is the allocation itself, for example a balanced fund with a bond portion, a larger cash reserve for near-term spending, or a smaller monthly amount that the budget can sustain through an income interruption. Regular investing does not avoid losses or guarantee a lower cost per unit. It does keep each deposit’s purchase date tied to when money is earned rather than to a forecast. Read the selected fund’s Fund Facts for its risk rating, fees and holdings, and review the account’s contribution and withdrawal rules separately. The companion guides on exiting and re-entering the market and keeping a cash floor beside regular purchases test related rules.
documents.keywords: Waiting for a dip before investing each paycheque: test the rule against regular purchases Hold new monthly savings in cash until the market falls by a set amount, or invest each deposit as it arrives. Compare the cash queue, the purchase prices and the ending value across three authored paths.

documents.keywords: The waiting rule buys only when the index is below the trigger line The index starts at 100. The trigger line follows the highest close observed so far, so a late dip can still occur at a higher level than earlier prices. This path invests waiting cash 8 times; its average cost per unit is 103.93 versus 101.25 for buying every month.

documents.keywords: The same rule can help, hurt or never fire depending on the path Every row uses the same deposits, trigger, waiting limit, cash rate and return scale; only the authored path changes. The three paths are not equally likely and are not a backtest. The rule is known in advance and uses only closes already observed.

documents.title: 股市崩盘之后，平衡组合需要一条规则：比较再平衡与任其漂移
documents.description: 跟随一个 60/40 投资组合经历崩盘、回升和第二次下跌。看看股票占比如何漂移、再平衡交易买入和卖出什么，以及这条规则何时有帮助、何时有损害。
documents.body: A crash lowers the equity share of a balanced portfolio. Rebalancing buys equity after the fall to restore the risk level you chose; it helped in the authored recovery and added to losses when a second decline followed. Inside a balanced fund the manager does this for you, while in a self-managed non-registered account the trades can have tax consequences. A crash changes the mix before it changes your plan A balanced portfolio holds equities and bonds in a chosen proportion. When equities fall much more than bonds, the equity share shrinks even though nobody traded. In the default scenario, a CAD 100,000 portfolio at 60% equity loses 35% on equity and gains 2% on bonds in year one. It ends the year at CAD 79,800 , with only 48.9% in equity. FINRA describes rebalancing as adjusting periodically to stay near a target allocation, by redirecting new money, adding to lagging assets or selling part of outperforming holdings. It also says there is no official timeline for when to rebalance and suggests considering it as part of an annual review. The first chart shows both portfolios’ equity share after any year-end trade. Rebalancing after a crash means buying what just fell The rebalanced portfolio trades back to 60% when equity is more than five percentage points off target at a year-end. After the crash, it sells about CAD 8,880 of bonds and buys equity. That is uncomfortable by design: the rule follows the allocation, not the headlines. The trade chart shows each year-end purchase or sale. During the recovery the equity share rises again, so later trades sell equity. Over the default ten years, the rebalanced portfolio buys about CAD 8,880 of equity and sells about CAD 11,834. Inside a balanced mutual fund or asset-allocation fund, the portfolio manager rebalances within the fund according to its mandate. You do not place those trades, but they can still affect the fund’s taxable distributions in a non-registered account. In a self-managed non-registered account, CRA’s capital gains guide explains that disposing of capital property such as fund units or shares can produce a capital gain or loss. Within a TFSA, income earned is generally tax-free, and in an RRSP tax is generally deferred until withdrawal. The account’s tax rules belong to the wrapper, not the fund. Recovery helps the rebalanced mix; a second decline hurts it first The value chart follows both portfolios. With three 15% equity recovery years and 6% afterwards, the default rebalanced portfolio ends at about CAD 142,505 , versus CAD 137,373 for the drifting portfolio. It held more equity when equities recovered. The variant chart changes the order of returns. If year two brings a second, smaller decline of 17.5% before the recovery, the rebalanced portfolio has already bought equity and its year-end value falls to about CAD 72,379 , versus CAD 74,199 for the drifting mix. It still ends ahead in that variant only because a recovery is assumed afterwards. With no crash, the drifting portfolio’s equity share rises to about 67% and it ends slightly higher, CAD 161,208 versus CAD 160,715, while carrying more equity risk than its target. No rule guarantees a better outcome. Rebalancing is mainly a way to keep the portfolio’s risk close to the level you chose, rather than letting recent returns choose it. Choose the band, the calendar and the cash source in advance Set the band to zero to rebalance at every year-end. A wider band trades less often and lets the mix move further before acting. Every trade can involve costs, spreads, sales charges or tax in a non-registered account; this model deducts none of them, so its results flatter frequent trading. New contributions can do some of the work without sales. Directing a regular deposit to the underweight asset can close part of the gap, as shown in the buy-only rebalancing guide . If you are withdrawing money, choosing which asset to sell can also move the mix; see withdrawal sale sources . A plan for crash worry that does not depend on predicting the crash Choose a target mix you could hold through a large equity decline, given your horizon, income and other cash. Keep near-term spending money outside the long-term portfolio. Write the rebalancing rule: calendar date, band and whether new contributions are used first. For a fund, read the Fund Facts and prospectus for its target mix, rebalancing approach, fees and risk rating. For a self-managed account, check the tax effect of each sale outside registered plans before trading. Review the mix after a major life change, not after each market headline. The balanced-fund stress guide adds inflation and fees to a crash scenario, and the loss-recovery guide separates recovering a dollar balance from recovering purchasing power.
documents.keywords: After a stock-market crash, a balanced mix needs a rule: compare rebalancing with drift Follow a 60/40 portfolio through a crash, a recovery and a second decline. See how the equity share drifts, what rebalancing trades buy and sell, and when the rule helps or hurts.

documents.title: 除非有东西把它恢复，崩盘会缩小股票占比
documents.parentTitle: 股市崩盘之后，平衡组合需要一条规则：比较再平衡与任其漂移
documents.description: 目标为 60% 股票。5 个百分点的再平衡区间允许小幅偏离而不交易。漂移组合从不交易，因此其股票占比随相对回报变动。
documents.body: 目标为 60% 股票。5 个百分点的再平衡区间允许小幅偏离而不交易。漂移组合从不交易，因此其股票占比随相对回报变动。
documents.keywords: A crash shrinks the equity share unless something restores it The target is 60% equity. A rebalancing band of 5 percentage points allows small deviations without a trade. The drifting mix never trades, so its equity share moves with relative returns.

documents.title: 有再平衡与没有再平衡的投资组合价值
documents.parentTitle: 股市崩盘之后，平衡组合需要一条规则：比较再平衡与任其漂移
documents.description: 两条线在第一年下跌的幅度相同，因为起始权重相同。之后的差异只来自崩盘后各自持有的股票占比。在回升期间，下跌后买入股票可能有帮助；如果下跌持续，同样的交易会加大亏损。
documents.body: 两条线在第一年下跌的幅度相同，因为起始权重相同。之后的差异只来自崩盘后各自持有的股票占比。在回升期间，下跌后买入股票可能有帮助；如果下跌持续，同样的交易会加大亏损。
documents.keywords: Portfolio value with and without rebalancing Both lines fall by the same amount in year one because they start with the same weights. Later differences come only from the equity share each holds after the crash. In a recovery, buying equity after the fall can help; if declines continue, the same trades add to losses.

documents.title: 再平衡交易：年末买入（+）或卖出（−）的股票
documents.parentTitle: 股市崩盘之后，平衡组合需要一条规则：比较再平衡与任其漂移
documents.description: 正值柱表示卖出债券买入股票；负值柱表示卖出股票买入债券。在非注册账户中，卖出可能构成处置，从而实现资本收益或亏损。在平衡型共同基金内，由基金本身进行交易，而其分配在注册计划以外仍可能需要纳税。此处未扣除税款和成本。
documents.body: 正值柱表示卖出债券买入股票；负值柱表示卖出股票买入债券。在非注册账户中，卖出可能构成处置，从而实现资本收益或亏损。在平衡型共同基金内，由基金本身进行交易，而其分配在注册计划以外仍可能需要纳税。此处未扣除税款和成本。
documents.keywords: Rebalancing trades: equity bought (+) or sold (−) at year-end A positive bar sells bonds to buy equity; a negative bar sells equity to buy bonds. In a non-registered account, a sale can be a disposition that realizes a capital gain or loss. Inside a balanced mutual fund, the fund itself trades, and its distributions may still be taxable outside a registered plan. Taxes and costs are not deducted here.

documents.title: 再平衡是一条风险控制规则，而不是有保证的回报提升
documents.parentTitle: 股市崩盘之后，平衡组合需要一条规则：比较再平衡与任其漂移
documents.description: “第二个下跌年度”变体把第二年改为第一年股票回报的一半，然后才开始回升。“没有崩盘”变体在每一年都使用之后年度的股票回报。期末价值取决于回报出现的顺序；任何变体都不是概率或预测。
documents.body: “第二个下跌年度”变体把第二年改为第一年股票回报的一半，然后才开始回升。“没有崩盘”变体在每一年都使用之后年度的股票回报。期末价值取决于回报出现的顺序；任何变体都不是概率或预测。
documents.keywords: Rebalancing is a risk-control rule, not a guaranteed return improvement The second-down-year variant replaces year two with half the year-one equity return, then begins the recovery. The no-crash variant uses the later equity return in every year. Ending values depend on the order of returns; no variant is a probability or forecast.

documents.title: 较低的燃油消耗评级仍然会产生较高的年度燃油费用
documents.description: 将 L/100 公里换算成每年的升数和现金，比较不同的燃油价格，并绘制城市/高速公路距离组合如何扭转结果的图表。
documents.body: 使用相同的行驶距离、支持的消耗估算以及每辆车所需的燃油价格来比较燃油现金。较低的每 100 公里升数只能回答该问题的一部分。在将标签复制到预算之前先阅读单位车辆的油耗等级描述了一段距离内使用的燃料。家庭燃料预算还需要行驶公里数和燃料价格。将一项评级与其他输入进行比较可能会得出错误的现金结论。加拿大自然资源部的 EnerGuide 解释称，综合消费评级反映了 55% 的城市驾驶和 45% 的高速公路驾驶。其年度燃油成本说明使用综合评级、20,000 公里和规定的燃油价格。这些约定可以帮助读者比较标签；它们并不是对任何特定家庭驾驶情况的衡量标准。这里的可编辑示例使用发明的车辆和燃料价格。车辆 A 在城市条件下分配为 10 升/100 公里，在高速公路上分配为 6 升/100 公里，每升 1.70 加元。 B在城市分配7，在高速公路分配7.5，每升1.95加元。这些既不是真实的制造商评级，也不是当前的泵价格。选择对比图案以使算术可见。按公里数而不是驾驶时间来衡量消耗量 默认的年行驶里程为 20,000 公里，其中城市条件下为 55%。这意味着 11,000 城市公里和 9,000 高速公路公里。相关重量是距离，因为消耗单位是每 100 公里升。将 55% 的驾驶时间花在交通上本身并不会产生相同的距离划分。对于A，选择的加权消耗量为10 × 0.55 + 6 × 0.45 = 8.2 L/100 km 。 B 为 7 × 0.55 + 7.5 × 0.45 = 7.225 L/100 km 。第一个图表将城市、高速公路和选定的混合比较分开。其标签将消费四舍五入到小数点后一位，而现金计算则保持完全精确。不要使用城市和高速公路数据的简单平均值，除非距离实际上是 50/50。同样，该说明性加权平均值并不试图根据四舍五入的已发布输入重建官方综合评级。使用支持的评级和适当的使用假设进行实际比较。将加权费率转换为年升，然后每年现金 转换为年升 = 年公里 ÷ 100 × 加权 L/100 公里 。单位很重要：直接将比率乘以 20,000 而不除以 100 会将燃料使用量夸大一百倍。因此，A 使用 20,000 ÷ 100 × 8.2 = 1,640 升。 B 使用 20,000 ÷ 100 × 7.225 = 1,445 升。在相同的假设距离内，B 的油耗减少了 195 升，比 A 少约 11.89%。应用每个输入的价格后，A 的年度燃油预算为 2,788 加元，B 为 2,817.75 加元。尽管 B 使用的燃油较少，但其燃油现金却高出 29.75 加元。差异在于每升 B 使用需支付 1.95 加元，而不是 1.70 加元。第二张图表将每个总计分为城市和高速公路公里的燃料。这些部分是同一年不同部分的成本，因此可以添加它们。升和美元不堆叠在一起。标题差异为 A 减去 B：正结果意味着 B 成本较低，而默认的负数 29.75 加元意味着 A 仅燃料成本较低。消费交叉和现金交叉不必同时发生。合成车辆在这两种情况下具有不同的优势。 A 在高速公路上每公里使用的燃料较少，而 B 在城市中使用的燃料较少。他们的距离加权消费率在城市份额为三分之一时相等：6 + 4w = 7.5 − 0.5w，其中 w 是城市距离分数。燃料现金使用不同的等式，因为每个费率都乘以自己的价格。 A 每百公里 10.20 加元 + 6.80w 加元； B 费用为每 100 公里 CAD 14.625 - CAD 0.975w。它们在 w = 4.425 ÷ 7.775 时相等，即大约 56.91% 的城市距离。在这两种份额之间，B 使用的升数较少，但 A 的燃油现金仍然较低。签名折线图重点关注现金比较及其零交叉。等式描述了输入的价格和消费模式；它没有为任何类型的车辆设定通用的城市驾驶门槛。如果两种成本模式相同，则每种组合都相关。其他输入可能在完全高速公路和完全城市驾驶之间没有任何平等。该模型明确说明了这些情况。在年距离为零的情况下，无论混合如何，两种燃料预算都为零。分别改变驾驶组合和燃油价格将城市距离从 55% 提高到 80%，保持总公里数和两个价格固定。 A 的加权使用量变为 9.2 L/100 km，B 的加权使用量为 7.1。他们每年的燃油成本分别为 3,128 加元和 2,769 加元，因此 B 现在的燃油成本减少了 359 加元。或者，保留默认的 55% 城市分割，但将 B 的假设燃油价格更改为 1.70 加元。 B 的燃油预算变为 2,456.50 加元，比 A 低 331.50 加元。该测试隔离了价格；事先测试隔离使用。两者都没有证明不同的燃油等级适合真实的车辆。该矩阵会改变城市距离份额和 B 的燃油价格。其固定案例是一种比较辅助工具，而不是对当地价格的预测。年公里数加倍会使所有建模的燃油现金和差异加倍，但当价格和消费保持固定时，它不会改变独特的城市份额交叉。将插图替换为实际车辆和路线的证据 加拿大自然资源部解释说，标准化测试评级并不能涵盖所有道路状况。驾驶行为、天气、交通、车辆状况和动力配件都会影响实际消耗。该工具不会估计这些影响或添加通用调整百分比。对于家庭计划，记录支持的燃料需求、相关评级或测量消耗、预期距离和日期的价格假设。路线变更可能会改变总公里数和城市/高速公路组合。明确测试这些效果，而不是仅更改单个组合评级。本页比较燃料支出。购买价格、贷款利息、折旧、维护、保险、停车和最终转售属于更广泛的车辆预算。仅凭良好的燃油结果并不能降低总拥有成本或证明购买溢价合理。相关的所有权和维修指南解决了这些不同的现金决策。
documents.keywords: A lower fuel-consumption rating can still produce a higher annual fuel bill Translate L/100 km into annual litres and cash, compare different fuel prices, and chart how a city/highway distance mix can reverse the result.

documents.title: 消费评级和所选的距离加权混合是单独的比较
documents.parentTitle: 较低的燃油消耗评级仍然会产生较高的年度燃油费用
documents.description: 所选组合根据输入的公里数份额对每个城市评级进行加权，并根据剩余份额对高速公路评级进行加权。除非城市距离为 50%，否则它不是相等的平均值。这些是原始消耗假设，未发布或重建的制造商评级。数值显示为一位小数；年度燃油成本使用完整加权结果。
documents.body: 所选组合根据输入的公里数份额对每个城市评级进行加权，并根据剩余份额对高速公路评级进行加权。除非城市距离为 50%，否则它不是相等的平均值。这些是原始消耗假设，未发布或重建的制造商评级。数值显示为一位小数；年度燃油成本使用完整加权结果。
documents.keywords: Consumption ratings and the selected distance-weighted mix are separate comparisons The selected mix weights each city rating by the entered share of kilometres and the highway rating by the remaining share. It is not an equal average unless city distance is 50%. These are original consumption assumptions, not published or reconstructed manufacturer ratings. Values display to one decimal; annual fuel costs use the full weighted result.

documents.parentTitle: 较低的燃油消耗评级仍然会产生较高的年度燃油费用
documents.description: 每个部分等于该条件下的公里数 × L/100 公里消耗量 ÷ 100 × 车辆特定的每升加元价格。该分部总额仅为年度燃油现金。两辆车行驶的距离相同。当所需的燃料更昂贵时，较低的总升数仍然会花费更多。价格并未确定任何实际车辆可以使用的燃油等级。
documents.body: 每个部分等于该条件下的公里数 × L/100 公里消耗量 ÷ 100 × 车辆特定的每升加元价格。该分部总额仅为年度燃油现金。两辆车行驶的距离相同。当所需的燃料更昂贵时，较低的总升数仍然会花费更多。价格并未确定任何实际车辆可以使用的燃油等级。
documents.keywords: Fuel cash depends on litres consumed and the price paid for each vehicle’s fuel Each segment equals kilometres in that condition × consumption in L/100 km ÷ 100 × the vehicle-specific CAD-per-litre price. The segment sum is annual fuel cash only. Both vehicles cover the same distance. A lower total number of litres can still cost more when the required fuel is more expensive. The prices do not establish which fuel grade any actual vehicle can use.

documents.description: 只有城市距离份额沿该曲线变化；总公里数、所有四种消耗投入和两种燃料价格均保持固定。零意味着每年的燃油现金相等。在这个有限的比较中，负值有利于 A。如果存在精确可行的等成本点，则将其包括在内。这是确定性成本关系，而不是驾驶或未来价格的概率分布。

documents.evidence: 假设的驱动组合敏感性
documents.keywords: The signed fuel-cost difference can reverse as the city-distance share changes Only the city-distance share changes along this curve; total kilometres, all four consumption inputs and both fuel prices stay fixed. Zero means equal annual fuel cash. Negative values favour A within this limited comparison. An exact feasible equal-cost point is included when one exists. This is a deterministic cost relationship, not a probability distribution of driving or future prices.

documents.keywords: Test the fuel-price difference beside the driving mix Columns replace vehicle B’s fuel price and rows replace city share of annual kilometres. Vehicle A’s price, annual distance and all consumption inputs stay selected values. Positive cells mean B has lower annual fuel cost and negative cells mean A does. The grid has no likelihood weights and does not quote local pump prices. At zero annual kilometres every cell is zero.

documents.title: 加薪、额外税收和福利逐步取消：比较完整的前后变化
documents.description: 四个图表将假设的固定收入税与实际收入税分开现金福利逐步取消，然后将当地边际冲抵额与整个加薪过程中保留的金额进行比较。
documents.body: 计算两个收入端点的税收和福利。适用于下一美元的利率可能与跨越逐步淘汰边界的加息的平均冲抵不同。分别定义收入税和现金福利 总工资上涨的变化可能比收入税的变化更大。如果一项单独的现金福利随着收入的增加而减少，则保留的金额也可能取决于该福利的逐步取消范围。经合组织关于工作激励的讨论解释了高税收和减少支持之间的普遍相互作用。这里的例子说明了发明系统的算术。它不复制任何经合组织国家使用的费率、家庭类型或规则。该模式对所有月度总收入征收 20% 的固定税。每月 300 加元的单独现金福利在总收入 1,500 加元的范围内保持最高。高于该固定阈值，每增加 1 美元，汇率就会下跌 0.50 加元，直到达到零。在这个虚构的系统中，假定福利是免税的，并且两笔金额都是在同一个模型月份收到的。没有括号、津贴、工资缴款、评估滞后或税收结算。每月资源定义为总收入减去模型税收加上模型福利。使用两个端点调节选定的加薪起始总收入为每月 2,000 加元。统一税为 400 加元。福利已从 300 加元降至 50 加元，因为 500 加元的收入高于起征点，导致 250 加元的逐步淘汰。因此，起始建模资源为 1,650 加元。每月总收入增加 200 加元，收入达到 2,200 加元。税收增加到 440 加元，而福利却为零。加注后模型资源为 1,760 加元。变化为总增长 200 加元 – 40 加元额外税 – 50 加元福利损失 = 110 加元。瀑布将这三项变化视为一种协调，而不是将福利减少视为另一项所得税费用。损失的福利上限为该人在加薪之前仍然收到的福利。对所有 200 加元实行 50% 逐步淘汰将错误地扣除 100 加元，即使只剩下 50 加元的福利。淘汰率需要起始平衡和终点。区分下一美元冲抵和全额加薪冲抵 在默认起始收入为 2,000 加元的情况下，下一个小额增长位于福利的逐步淘汰范围内。右边的当地冲抵额是 20% 的额外税收加上 50% 的福利减少，即 70%。在该细分市场中，额外总收入的 1 加元会为建模资源增加 0.30 加元。全额加薪 200 加元，超过福利耗尽点（2,100 加元）。第一个 100 加元保留 30 加元。下一个 100 加元没有进一步的损失，在相同的统一税后保留 80 加元。这些部分总共保留 110 加元。额外税费加上损失的福利总计 90 加元，在 200 加元的总加薪基础上冲抵了 45%。所选变更的平均值与起点时的 70% 本地比率不同。因此，总体比率使用整个选定的增长作为其分母。它不是所有收入的平均税负，也不会自动成为适用于每一美元的边际税率。如果总增长为零，则该比率未定义并显示为 N/A。资源水平和资源增加回答不同的问题 第一个图表绘制了模型资源水平与总收入的关系。其两条线之间的差距就是当前的效益。当差距缩小时，效益就为零；这不是第二次纳税或新的工资扣除。该曲线包括确切的逐步淘汰开始点和耗尽点（当后者落在图表内时）。这些是斜率的变化。虚构的福利不断下降，因此该模型不会造成突然的资格悬崖。相反，起始收入比较保持总增长固定，并从几个起点重新计算收益。高于逐步淘汰范围的行可以保留更多相同的加薪，因为没有任何好处可以损失。更大的增量收益并不意味着高收入情景会获得更大的收益。它还没有比较完整的家庭生活水平。阅读资源级别图表以及变化，而不是将一个增益条解释为总预算。保留边界情况，而不是强迫一个有利的答案 零淘汰率使效益保持在输入的最大值不变。零效益完全消除了淘汰渠道。无论哪种情况，总增长都只能通过虚构的固定收入税来改变资源。好处永远不会变成负数。一旦耗尽，它就无法随着收入的增长而继续减少资源。在逐步淘汰开始时，显示的右侧本地汇率包括下一美元的减少；在耗尽时，它排除了任何进一步的减少。控件还允许故意进行极端组合。在积极逐步淘汰的细分市场内，采用 60% 的统一税和 100% 的福利削减率，当地冲抵额合计为 160%。完全在该细分市场内额外增加 100 CAD 将会减少 60 CAD 的建模资源。图表保留了此类负面变化。它们描述了输入的虚构规则，而不是真实国家拒绝额外工作的激励或建议。该计算不包括职业发展、养老金应计、工作成本、非现金服务或家庭偏好。在使用预算数字之前验证实际评估期 该矩阵会改变起始收入和总增长规模，同时保留输入的税收和福利假设。每个单元格都会重新计算两个端点。在不检查利益是否仍然存在的情况下，它不会跨越边界扩展一种当地税率。真正的比较需要实际的收入定义、适用的家庭情况、评估期限和领取时间。基于较早纳税年度的福利可能会在与工资收入不同的日期做出答复。预扣税变更也可能与最终税款不同。这些细节在这张特意绘制的同月插图中没有出现。在更改支出或储蓄承诺之前，请获取适用的规则和确认的金额，然后将收据和义务放在实际日期。这里的资源变化不是银行余额或负担能力的发现。有用的习惯是将总增加额与每项额外税款或损失的付款分别进行核对。保持分母可见，将局部斜率与完全变化比率区分开来，并在实际剩余效益处停止效益减少。这使得工资变动的影响在纳入家庭计划之前就可以理解。

documents.title: 通过福利的开始和结束跟踪资源水平逐步淘汰

documents.description: 曲线包含图表内精确的固定逐步淘汰开始点和任何有限耗尽点，因此线段不会平滑斜率的变化。两条线的区别在于当前福利，而不是其他工资支付。该图显示了不同总收入情景中的资源水平，而不是职业预测。

documents.keywords: Reconcile the selected gross raise with extra tax and the benefit lost The benefit loss is limited to what was still received at the starting income. Its phase-out rate is not applied without limit to the whole raise. This change identity equals after-raise resources minus before-raise resources; it does not calculate the household’s total budget or an actual tax bill.

documents.keywords: The same gross raise can retain different amounts at different starting incomes Only starting gross earnings are replaced. The selected raise, tax rate, maximum benefit, phase-out rate and fixed threshold stay unchanged. Each row compares its own before/after resources. A larger gain from a different starting income does not establish a higher benefit or compare overall living standards.

documents.keywords: Test a complete before-and-after change across both starting income and raise size Rows replace starting monthly gross earnings; columns replace the monthly gross increase. Both endpoints are recalculated using the selected tax, benefit and phase-out assumptions. These are dollar changes, not local marginal percentages or resource levels. A negative cell is preserved when the invented combined deductions exceed the gross increase.

documents.title: 债券价格估算误差有多少？绘制持续时间背后的曲线
documents.description: 四个图表将准确的年度现金流重新定价与久期和凸度估计进行比较，协调剩余误差并测试不同的期限和收益率变动。
documents.body: 修正持续时间给出局部直线估计。凸性增加了二阶修正，而精确的重新定价仍然可以检查这些近似值遗漏的内容。有用的敏感性仍然是近似值。久期数字压缩了债券对其收益率微小变化的敏感性。它对于初步了解价格风险很有用，但它通过弯曲的关系画出一条直线。考虑一张面额为 100,000 加元、年息 5% 且剩余期限为 10 年的原始假设债券。按年有效收益率 5% 计算，扣除十张息票和最终本金后，初始价值为 100,000 加元。这里的问题很狭窄：如果它自己的收益率立即发生变化，那么两个局部近似值与再次贴现每笔剩余付款的接近程度如何？ CFA 协会的公开凸性概述将凸性描述为非线性价格-收益率关系的补充指标。这些图表使用独立的现金流量和计算来使差异可见。保持付款固定并更改折扣率 优惠券每年 5,000 加元。去年还返还了10万加元面值。模型价格是每笔付款的总和除以一加上年收益率，再加上该付款之前的年数。将收益率提高两个百分点，从 5% 提高到 7%。将所有付款重新定价为 7% 约为 85,952.84 加元。与原始值的瞬时变化约为-14.0472%。这里的“精确”是指在选定的贴现现金流模型中精确。这并不意味着债券交易商会以该价格执行。该计算假设每次付款均已完成，对所有日期应用一个年收益率，并且不包括交易成本或付款条件的变化。使用起始修改持续时间绘制切线该示例计算出的修改持续时间约为 7.72173 。其一阶价格变化估计为 - 初始价格 × 修改久期 × 收益率变化。两个百分点的变动输入为 0.02 ，而不是 2 。估计的变化约为 −CAD 100,000 × 7.72173 × 0.02 = −CAD 15,443.47 。这样，仅久期的估计值为 CAD 84,556.53 。直接估计值比模型的准确值低 1,396.31 加元。因此，它预测此次收益率上升将造成太大损失。价格曲线图显示切线和精确的重新定价曲线在起始收益率处相遇，并随着波动的增长而分离。添加收益率移动平方的二阶修正 该示例的年凸度（使用相对于收益率的导数作为分数）约为 74.99768 。二阶美元调整为 ½ × 初始价格 × 凸度 × 收益率变化² 。对于 0.02 的变动，调整约为 +CAD 1,499.95 。将其添加到仅久期值中，两项估计值将变为 CAD 86,056.48 。在本例中，该价格更接近，但仍比准确的重新定价高出 103.65 加元。二阶近似不会仅仅因为包含曲率项而成为精确的估值。其剩余差异在标题指标和瀑布图中仍然可见。调整和残差是估值项，而不是收入瀑布从 100,000 加元开始，减去久期 15,443.47 加元，加上凸性 1,499.95 加元，并减去剩余的 103.65 加元修正。它以精确的 CAD 85,952.84 模型值结束。这些步骤都不会将现金存入帐户。凸度调整是两个价格估计之间的差异，而不是优惠券、贡献或报销。残差是协调该模型重新定价的近似值所需的差值。该计算也不会将日历提前。在瞬时冲击之后，该债券还有十年的期限。尚未收到或再投资任何优惠券。一年期总回报比较需要稍后的剩余期限、当年支付的现金以及对这些收入的处理。收益率向上和向下的相同变动并不需要产生相同的美元变化。当收益率变动逆转时，久期期限会改变符号。对于这种固定支付、无期权债券，凸度项保持为正值，因为变动是平方的并且其计算出的凸度为正值。对于两个百分点的下降，仅久期估计给出的结果约为+15.4435%。添加相同的二阶校正大约可得到 +16.9434%。对于上涨，两项估计值约为-13.9435%。这些是围绕相同起始产量的当地估计；准确的重新定价仍然是比较。这种不对称性源于所选固定现金流价格函数的曲率。它不应自动应用于可赎回债券或其他付款可能随利率变动而变化的工具。该计算器没有对嵌入期权进行建模，也不会估计投资组合不断变化的信用利差或非平行收益率曲线。将到期网格视为近似误差图 该网格会更改剩余期限和收益率变动，同时保留选定的面额、票面金额和起始收益率。每个到期日都有自己的初始价格和修改后的期限，然后将其本地估计与准确的重新定价进行比较。其单元格是仅持续时间的估计值减去精确模型值。负数表示切线位于精确曲线下方。对于可能意味着夸大损失的向上冲击；对于下行冲击，这可能意味着低估的收益。这些数字是所选头寸规模的美元误差。将面部数量加倍即可使它们加倍，而不会改变百分比灵敏度。该网格没有指定移动的概率，也没有说明较长的债券适合家庭的消费日期。使用目标付款日期旁边的近似检查 计划在到期前出售的家庭需要考虑可能的价格变化下的可用现金。方便的久期估计可以作为起始敏感性，而较大的变动则需要仔细研究实际付款和合适的估值模型。持有债券至合同到期会改变规划问题，但不会使其中期价值保持不变。流动性需求、违约风险和息票再投资仍然很重要。该模型的数学压力，包括任何负结果收益率，不提供实际的产品报价或承诺的未来机会。确认付款时间表和费率约定。以分数或百分点一致地表达产量变化。计算指定起点的持续时间和凸度。将当地估计值与重新定价的现金流量进行比较。在将结果用于现金目标之前先调节剩余误差。
documents.keywords: How much does a bond-price estimate miss? Draw the curve behind duration Four charts compare exact annual-cash-flow repricing with duration and convexity estimates, reconcile the remaining error and test different maturities and yield moves.

documents.title: 准确的价格收益率曲线偏离久期切线
documents.parentTitle: 债券价格估算误差有多少？绘制持续时间背后的曲线
documents.description: 横轴围绕选定的起始收益率改变债券自身的年度有效收益率，从 -3 个百分点到 +3 个百分点。票面金额、息票和剩余期限保持固定。所有三个曲线均在零移动处匹配。直接估计使用起始修改持续时间；曲线估计还保留起始凸性。这两种估计都不会更新每个绘制收益率的敏感性。
documents.body: 横轴围绕选定的起始收益率改变债券自身的年度有效收益率，从 -3 个百分点到 +3 个百分点。票面金额、息票和剩余期限保持固定。所有三个曲线均在零移动处匹配。直接估计使用起始修改持续时间；曲线估计还保留起始凸性。这两种估计都不会更新每个绘制收益率的敏感性。
documents.keywords: The exact price-yield curve bends away from the duration tangent The horizontal axis changes the bond’s own annual effective yield around the selected starting yield, from −3 to +3 percentage points. Face amount, coupon and remaining maturity stay fixed. All three curves match at a zero move. The straight estimate uses starting modified duration; the curved estimate also retains starting convexity. Neither estimate updates those sensitivities at each plotted yield.

With fixed positive cash flows and the supported yield domain, the price-yield curve is convex. The linear tangent lies below it. The second-order estimate can still be above or below exact repricing; its residual is not silently removed.

documents.title: 在近似条款和残差后协调准确的重新定价
documents.parentTitle: 债券价格估算误差有多少？绘制持续时间背后的曲线
documents.description: 期限为 - 初始价格 × 修改期限 × 收益变化。凸度项是 + 1/2 × 初始价格 × 凸度 × 收益率变化的平方。收益率变化是一个分数，因此 2 个百分点的变动将输入 0.02。最终修正等于准确的重新定价减去两项估计。每一步都是估值的变化；没有步骤将现金存入帐户。
documents.body: 期限为 - 初始价格 × 修改期限 × 收益变化。凸度项是 + 1/2 × 初始价格 × 凸度 × 收益率变化的平方。收益率变化是一个分数，因此 2 个百分点的变动将输入 0.02。最终修正等于准确的重新定价减去两项估计。每一步都是估值的变化；没有步骤将现金存入帐户。
documents.keywords: Reconcile the exact repricing after both approximation terms and the residual The duration term is −initial price × modified duration × yield change. The convexity term is +½ × initial price × convexity × yield change squared. Yield change is a fraction, so a 2-percentage-point move enters as 0.02. The final correction equals exact repricing minus the two-term estimate. Every step is a valuation change; no step pays cash into the account.

documents.keywords: A local duration estimate can leave a larger dollar error at longer maturities Rows replace years remaining and columns replace the yield change; each cell recalculates its own starting price and duration at that maturity. Face amount, coupon and starting yield remain selected. Negative cells mean the duration-only tangent underestimates the exact model value. The grid overrides the selected maturity and shock. It is an approximation-error comparison, not a return forecast or a measure of default risk.

documents.title: 美元投资需要有日期的加元成本记录：分别转换购买和销售
documents.description: 四个可编辑图形可分别调节换算的成本和收益，解释价格/货币分解，并强调加元结果，即使美元差额为零也是如此。
documents.body: 加元资本财产计算需要注明日期的加元收益、成本和费用。按一种汇率换算的美元利润可以忽略原始成本的货币变化。将成本和收益分开转换日期美元报表可以显示明确的利润，同时留下不完整的加元记录。支付的金额、销售收入和相关费用需要兼容的单位才能对账。 CRA的资本利得指引称，外币收益使用出售时的汇率进行兑换，调整后的成本基础使用购买时的汇率进行兑换，处置费用则使用发生时的汇率进行兑换。本文隔离了一次购买和随后的完整处置，之后没有调整成本变化。收购输入包括在同一购买日期发生的任何合格成本。处置费用在转换为 CAD 后单独输入。该示例不会通过多次采购或以后的调整来重建汇总成本基础。这里的所有费率都是发明的。加拿大央行的汇率页面将其外国报价表示为转换为加元的一外币单位，并将其描述为指示性平均值。该工具使用明确规定的报价方向，无需导入当前报价或假设银行将按指示性利率执行。协调 CAD 中的单次采购示例 编写的示例以 10,000 美元的采购成本和 1 美元的 1.25 CAD 的采购日期汇率开始。这将产生 10,000 × 1.25 的历史 CAD 成本，或 12,500 CAD。全部处置的收益总额为 12,000 美元。其单独输入的销售日期汇率为 1.35 加元兑 1 美元，折算后收益为 16,200 加元。符合条件的处置费用已转换并输入为 50 加元。因此，第一个瀑布计算为 16,200 加元减去 12,500 加元再减去 50 加元，在任何包含率或个人税计算之前获得 3,650 加元算术收益。每个数字都有自己的作用。购置金额是历史成本记录，折算收益描述处置价值，费用减少一次结果。这三个主要指标不应作为家庭资产加在一起。解释货币对原始成本的影响 本例中的美元变动是 12,000 减去 10,000，即 2,000 美元。仅按销售价格折算该差额，扣除加元费用即可得到 2,700 加元。它留下了过时的加元调节的另一部分未解释的内容。原来的 10,000 美元成本受到两个汇率之间变化的影响。乘以 1.35 减去 1.25 得到 1,000 加元。第二个瀑布将 2,700 加元和 1,000 加元相加，然后减去 50 加元费用，得到相同的 3,650 加元结果。这是一种精确的代数分解。美元变动术语按全部销售汇率换算，因此它已经包含了美元变动和货币变动之间的相互作用。添加另一个交互量会将部分结果计算两次。分解解释了记录。它不识别两个单独的存款、归因交易技能或计算实际货币对冲的收益。零美元差额并不要求零加元差额 将美元总收益设置为等于原始 10,000 美元购置成本，同时保留默认购置率、销售率和加元费用。美元差额为零。换算后的加元收益现为 13,500 加元。历史加元成本仍为 12,500 加元。扣除 50 加元费用后，算术加元收益为 950 加元。该结果不需要美元价格利润。签名金条保持等值美元条件并改变售价。按照 1 美元兑 1 加元的汇率计算，算术结果为负 2,550 加元。当收购率为 1.25 时，只有 50 加元的费用仍为负结果。如果售价为 1.50，算术收益为 2,450 加元。这些是单独的压力案例。负值并不自动构成合格的资本损失，并且该图表不测试限制、其他交易或特殊财产规则。它还没有为任何货币路径分配概率。根据自己的基础保留税务记录和银行现金计划 该矩阵会同时更改美元总收益和销售日期利率。其列标签是美元金额，行标签是加元兑美元汇率，单元格值是加元算术结果。原始购买日期成本保持不变。用于准备记录的 CAD 翻译并不能证明销售收入已兑换成 CAD。如果结算产生保留的美元现金，则该现金的后续交换或处置会在该模型之外产生另一个创纪录的问题。兑换利差、实际银行收据和支出日期需要有自己的分类账。计算器也会在税前停止。它不使用包含率、税级、损失扣除、外国税收抵免或退款估算。注册账户交易、收入账户处理、多个收购日期、再投资或后来的 ACB 调整将需要不同的范围。保留购买证据、其 CAD 转换、任何后续成本调整、销售证据和单独转换的费用​​。单一的当前汇率无法仅根据美元报表的净利润来重建历史。 2026 年 10 月 25 日审核的 CRA 页面包含 2025 年申报材料。它的转换框架支持这个有限的教育示例；该工具不准备回报或确定拟议交易的处理方式。
documents.keywords: A USD investment needs a dated CAD cost record: convert the purchase and sale separately Four editable graphics reconcile separately translated cost and proceeds, explain the price/currency decomposition and stress a CAD result even when the USD difference is zero.

documents.title: 在核对结果之前翻译每个日期金额
documents.parentTitle: 美元投资需要有日期的加元成本记录：分别转换购买和销售
documents.description: 加元成本是假设的单次购买调整后的成本基础，没有后续调整。收益和成本使用自己独立输入的费率。加元费用不会进行第二次换算。将美元收益换算为创纪录并不意味着银行实际上将销售现金转换为加元。
documents.body: 加元成本是假设的单次购买调整后的成本基础，没有后续调整。收益和成本使用自己独立输入的费率。加元费用不会进行第二次换算。将美元收益换算为创纪录并不意味着银行实际上将销售现金转换为加元。
documents.keywords: Translate each dated amount before reconciling the result The CAD cost is the assumed single-purchase adjusted cost base with no later adjustments. Proceeds and cost use their own independently entered rates. The CAD expense is not translated a second time. Translating USD proceeds for a record does not mean a bank actually converted the sale cash into CAD.

documents.title: 协调美元变化和货币影响，不重复计算
documents.parentTitle: 美元投资需要有日期的加元成本记录：分别转换购买和销售
documents.description: 一种精确的分解：（美元收益 - 原始美元成本）×销售率，加上原始美元成本×（销售率 - 收购率），减去加元费用。第一个术语已使用完整销售率，因此不会添加额外的价格/货币交互。这些是会计贡献，而不是单独收到的现金或衡量的对冲收益。
documents.body: 一种精确的分解：（美元收益 - 原始美元成本）×销售率，加上原始美元成本×（销售率 - 收购率），减去加元费用。第一个术语已使用完整销售率，因此不会添加额外的价格/货币交互。这些是会计贡献，而不是单独收到的现金或衡量的对冲收益。
documents.keywords: Reconcile the USD change and the currency effect without double counting One exact decomposition: (USD proceeds − original USD cost) × sale rate, plus original USD cost × (sale rate − acquisition rate), less the CAD expense. The first term already uses the full sale rate, so no extra price/currency interaction is added. These are accounting contributions, not separately received cash or a measured hedging payoff.

documents.title: 同等美元收益和成本仍可能产生加元损益
documents.parentTitle: 美元投资需要有日期的加元成本记录：分别转换购买和销售
documents.description: 每一行都将美元总收益替换为原始美元采购成本，使美元差异为零。输入的采购率、原始成本和 CAD 销售费用保持不变。这些行使用 80%、100% 和 120% 的收购率加上选定的销售率，计算前压力率四舍五入到小数点后四位，并删除重复率。货币换算和费用仍然会产生加元差异；不提供收益概率、应付税款或可扣除损失裁决。
documents.body: 每一行都将美元总收益替换为原始美元采购成本，使美元差异为零。输入的采购率、原始成本和 CAD 销售费用保持不变。这些行使用 80%、100% 和 120% 的收购率加上选定的销售率，计算前压力率四舍五入到小数点后四位，并删除重复率。货币换算和费用仍然会产生加元差异；不提供收益概率、应付税款或可扣除损失裁决。
documents.keywords: Equal USD proceeds and cost can still leave a CAD gain or loss Every row replaces USD gross proceeds with the original USD acquisition cost, making the USD difference zero. The entered acquisition rate, original cost and CAD selling expense stay fixed. The rows use 80%, 100% and 120% of the acquisition rate plus the selected sale rate, with stress rates rounded to four decimals before calculation and duplicate rates removed. Currency translation and the expense can still create a CAD difference; no gain probability, tax payable or deductible-loss ruling is supplied.

documents.title: 同时强调销售收益和销售日期利率
documents.parentTitle: 美元投资需要有日期的加元成本记录：分别转换购买和销售
documents.description: 原始美元购置成本、购置日期汇率和加元费用保持不变。栏目金额为美元收益；单元格值是包含税前的 CAD 结果。费率行使用 80% 和 120% 的获取率加上选定的销售率。美元收益栏使用选定收益的 75%、100% 和 125%；压力率四舍五入至小数点后四位，美元在计算前四舍五入至美分，并删除重复的情况。这些是作者撰写的压力，而不是市场报价或置信范围。负单元格仍然是算术损失，其资格需要单独审核。
documents.body: 原始美元购置成本、购置日期汇率和加元费用保持不变。栏目金额为美元收益；单元格值是包含税前的 CAD 结果。费率行使用 80% 和 120% 的获取率加上选定的销售率。美元收益栏使用选定收益的 75%、100% 和 125%；压力率四舍五入至小数点后四位，美元在计算前四舍五入至美分，并删除重复的情况。这些是作者撰写的压力，而不是市场报价或置信范围。负单元格仍然是算术损失，其资格需要单独审核。
documents.keywords: Stress the sale proceeds and the sale-date rate together The original USD acquisition cost, acquisition-date rate and CAD expense stay fixed. Column amounts are USD proceeds; cell values are CAD results before inclusion and tax. Rate rows use 80% and 120% of the acquisition rate plus the selected sale rate. USD proceeds columns use 75%, 100% and 125% of selected proceeds; stress rates are rounded to four decimals and USD proceeds to cents before calculation, with duplicate cases removed. These are authored stresses rather than market quotes or a confidence range. A negative cell remains an arithmetic loss whose eligibility requires separate review.

documents.title: 用电时间：比较您可以转移的能源和整个月度账单
documents.description: 保持每月总千瓦时不变，同时转移部分高峰使用，然后以简化的形式将节省的能源费用、不变的费用和百分比变化分开账单。
documents.body: 更便宜的价格仅适用于进入该时期的能源。在估计整个账单节省之前，使用消耗权重并保持不变的费用分开。确定时间变化会影响账单的哪一部分 较低的非高峰能源价格可能很有用，但它不会自动适用于每月账单上的每千瓦时或每笔费用。规划计算从可移动的能量和保持不变的电荷量开始。安大略能源委员会的账单解释将取决于使用时间的电费与其他账单组成部分区分开来。它还解释说，有些运费是固定的，而另一些则不同。这支持单独阅读账单的各个部分，而不是将整个发票视为一份能源价格。该工具使用简化的原始三期账单：假设能源价格为高峰 20 美分/千瓦时、中峰 12 美分、非高峰 8 美分，加上假设每月 20 加元不变。这些不是安大略省的当前价格或公用事业报价。其他可变运费、损失、需求费用、税费、等级和回扣均不在计算范围内。按实际使用情况衡量能源价格，而不是对费率标签进行平均 起始分配为高峰 280 千瓦时、中峰 210 千瓦时和非高峰 210 千瓦时，总计 700 千瓦时。能源成本分别为 56 加元、25.20 加元和 16.80 加元。添加它们会产生 98 加元的可变能量费用。消耗加权能源价格为 98 加元 ÷ 700 千瓦时，即 14 美分/千瓦时。这与三个费率标签的未加权平均值不同：(20 + 12 + 8) ÷ 3，即约 13.33 美分。该家庭在每个时期都没有使用相同的数量，因此相同的权重回答了不同的问题。添加未改变的CAD 20产生CAD 118的简化基线账单。固定金额有单独的作用；这不是另一个适用于 700 kWh 的能源费率。同样，这种仅能源加权费率并不是实际公用事业账单的完整总费率。高峰用电量的四分之一并非总用电量的四分之一 默认转换为原始高峰用电量 280 kWh 的 25%。这会将 70 千瓦时的电量移至非高峰时段。由于整个月有700度电，转移量仅占总用电量的10%。转变后，高峰和中峰用电量均为210千瓦时，非高峰用电量升至280千瓦时。总能量仍为 700 kWh。第一个图表使这种保护可见：从一个时期删除的金额出现在另一个时期，而不是从账单中消失。这是一个时间示例，而不是能源效率的改进。它假设移动选定的用途不会增加其他消耗、改变所提供的服务或需要设备支出。该工具无法确定特定家庭是否真的可以转移其部分使用量。从避免的电量中减去新电量 转移的 70 kWh 的费用为 70 × 0.20 加元 = 高峰时段 14 加元。非高峰期费用为 70 × 0.08 加元 = 5.60 加元。因此，每个模型月可节省 8.40 加元，即 70 千瓦时 × 0.12 加元的价差。瀑布使变化的双方都可见。避免原始电荷只是第一步；新时期能源仍需付出。比较两种分配时，未变化的费用和所有未移动的能源被取消。下班后能源费为 89.60 加元。在 20 CAD 不变的情况下，简化账单变为 109.60 CAD 。假定不支付或回扣 8.40 加元；该金额是相对于原始分配避免的现金支出。将分母保留在每个百分比旁边 在本示例中，非高峰单价比高峰单价低 60%：(20 − 8) ÷ 20。该比较适用于移动的 70 kWh 的价格，而不是所有 700 kWh 或完整的账单。可变能源费用下降 8.40 加元 ÷ 98 加元，即约 8.57%。简化后的整体账单下跌 8.40 加元 ÷ 118 加元，即约 7.12%。消耗加权能源价格从 14.0 美分/千瓦时变化至 12.8 美分/千瓦时，而总使用量保持不变。所有三个百分比都可以同时正确，因为它们的分母不同。将 60% 的单价降低描述为 60% 的账单节省，将对更大的基数进行有限的改变。将不变的每月金额从 20 加元增加到 60 加元，节省的金额仍为 8.40 加元。基准账单变为158加元，因此其减少百分比约为5.32%。费用不变会影响节省的账单份额，即使它不会改变能源成本差异。分别测试可实现的转变和价差 最终图表将原始高峰使用比例从 0 更改为 100%，同时保持输入的数量、费率和不变费用不变。原始法案仍然是参考线。在零位移时，两个钞票重合；由于没有高峰使用，每个班次设置都有相同的结果。期间名称本身并不强制算术中的较低价格。如果输入的非高峰费率超过高峰费率，则移动能源会提高建模费用，并且节省指标变为负数。如果两个速率匹配，仅靠计时并不能节省能源。仅更改选定的班次会更新标题结果和分配栏，同时保留全范围比较曲线。该曲线并未指定任何数量的转移使用的可能性，也没有确定家用电器可以实现的目标。在将储蓄纳入家庭计划之前使用实际账单 从账单中记录相关能源数量和价格周期。确定可行的移动用量，而不是假设每千瓦时都可以移动。将不变的费用与所有其他变化的费用分开。比较完整的适用关税和任何转换或设备成本。在预测年度节省之前回顾不同的季节。 12 个相同的示例月份将节省 100.80 加元的时间。这是重复案例的计算，而不是年度预测：使用量、费率、期间定义和可移动的金额在一年中可能会有所不同。该插图并不比较实际的电力计划或确定其资格。它解释了选定的时间变化如何通过故意简单的法案。相关的公用事业支付和升级指南解决了有关支付时间表和能源使用变化的不同问题。
documents.keywords: Time-of-use electricity: compare the energy you can shift and the whole monthly bill Hold total monthly kWh constant while moving part of on-peak use, then separate energy-charge savings, unchanged fees and the percentage change in a simplified bill.

documents.title: 相同的总能源分配给不同的计费周期
documents.parentTitle: 用电时间：比较您可以转移的能源和整个月度账单
documents.description: 转变百分比适用于原来的高峰千瓦时，而不是所有家庭用电。删除的高峰时段金额将准确添加到非高峰时段，而中峰时段保持不变。这是时间替代，而不是能源效率节省或测量的家庭使用情况。
documents.body: 转变百分比适用于原来的高峰千瓦时，而不是所有家庭用电。删除的高峰时段金额将准确添加到非高峰时段，而中峰时段保持不变。这是时间替代，而不是能源效率节省或测量的家庭使用情况。
documents.keywords: The same total energy is allocated to different billing periods The shift percentage applies to the original on-peak kWh, not to all household consumption. The removed on-peak amount is added to off-peak exactly, while mid-peak stays unchanged. This is timing substitution, not an energy-efficiency saving or a measured household usage profile.

documents.evidence: 假设的简化账单组成部分
documents.keywords: Energy charges change while the entered fixed amount stays the same The variable energy segment adds each period’s kWh multiplied by its entered price. The second segment is the unchanged monthly input. This is a deliberately limited bill, not a complete representation of an actual utility’s delivery, regulatory, loss, tax or rebate calculations. A percentage reduction in one unit price does not apply to both entire bars.

Unshifted energy and the unchanged monthly amount cancel in the comparison. The endpoint is a cost reduction relative to the original allocation, not a cash payment from the utility. A negative endpoint means the shifted allocation costs more.

documents.title: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 相反两个四年期等本贷款的年利率块，比较共同的债务路径和不同的现金支付，并协调为什么相同的平均利率并不意味着相同的成本。
documents.body: 适用时，利率乘以未偿债务。简单平均法会放弃这种配对，因此利率时机可能会改变总利息和家庭付款日历。将每个利率放在其适用的债务金额旁边。四年平均利率可以隐藏利率发生的顺序。如果本金在贷款期间下降，那么早年的高利率比临近年底的相同高利率适用的资金更多。因此，计算每种利率出现的频率不足以确定美元利息总额。加拿大金融消费者机构的个人贷款指南解释说，借款涉及本金、利息、付款条件和潜在费用。该图在使用其自己的简化还款规则的同时使这些组件保持独特。它不是贷款机构贷款报价的复制。该模型借款 24,000 加元，并在四年结束时偿还本金 6,000 加元。每年的利息在同一检查点单独支付。偿还的本金金额是固定的，而每年的还款总额则随着当年的利息而变化。反转利率块而不改变其算术平均数 A 块的假设年利率为 10%，B 块的假设年利率为 6%。 A-first 序列使用 10%、10%、6% 和 6%。 B优先序列使用6%、6%、10%和10%。每个序列在每个比率下都包含两年，因此两者的简单平均值均为 8%。这两种利率都不是报价或预测。交换顺序会留下相同的四个输入利率，但会改变满足较大早期贷款余额的利率。主要图表由两个序列共享。四个计息期的期初余额分别为 24,000 加元、18,000 加元、12,000 加元和 6,000 加元。最终偿还 6,000 加元本金后，贷款为零。余额中不会添加未付利息，并且这两个序列都不会仅仅因为其利息费用较低而获得更大的还款额。由于本金偿还每年进行一次，因此每年全年期初债务均未偿还。将每年还款额除以十二可能会建议每月进行储蓄分配，但不会将其转换为每月还款贷款。实际每月本金减少会改变利息计算，需要自己的时间表。计算每年期初余额的利息 在 A-first 情况下，前两笔利息分别为 2,400 加元和 1,800 加元。后面的 6% 利率适用于 12,000 加元和 6,000 加元，分别为 720 加元和 360 加元。总利息为 5,280 加元。在 B-first 情况下，较大的早期余额的 6% 产生 1,440 加元和 1,080 加元。后面的 10% 利率产生 1,200 加元和 600 加元。总利息为 4,320 加元。尽管匹配 8% 的简单平均值，但差异为 960 加元。瀑布每年从 A 优先利息中减去 B 优先利息。前两年加960加元和720加元，后两年减480加元和240加元。早期增加的金额超过了后来减少的金额，因为当应用早期利率差异时，更多的本金未偿还。在评估家庭现金日历时加回本金 利息是此处的借贷成本组成部分，但不是离开家庭帐户的全部金额。每每年还款还可以返还 6,000 加元的本金。付款条包括这两个部分，因此可以将其解读为现金需求。 A 级年付款分别为 8,400 加元、7,800 加元、6,720 加元和 6,360 加元。他们的总额为 29,280 加元：原始本金 24,000 加元加上利息 5,280 加元。 B-first 总额为 28,320 加元，包括相同的本金和 4,320 加元的利息。比较总成本时，共享主成分取消，但在每个到期日仍然需要资金。家庭不能只保留利息金额并假设贷款将会消失。此示例也不假设早期付款中节省的资金被投资、花费或用于额外的本金偿还。这些选择将改变建模的现金流量。另一种假设是对看似平均的债务应用平均利率，对实际四项期初余额使用 8% 的固定利率将产生 4,800 加元的利息。这是第三种不同的利率路径。它位于两个默认总计之间，但不等于其中任何一个。用平均值替换原始订单改变了计算方式。四项一年期风险敞口的四项期初余额总计为 60,000 加元。这并不意味着该家庭借了 60,000 加元：同样的贷款下降现象屡见不鲜。将每笔利息总额除以余额总和分别得出 8.8% 和 7.2%，从而使不同的余额权重可见。最后的百分比是本发明时间表的算术摘要，不是受监管的年利率、引用的年度借款成本或对到期付款进行评估的替代品。对于这个假设的基于余额的利息规则，在所有四年内对原始 24,000 加元全额应用 8% 将完全忽略本金偿还。明确使用固定原始本金基础的合同是一种不同的计算。使用利率对矩阵，而不将场景转化为预测 该矩阵替换了两个利率块，同时保留初始本金和四笔等额还款。正单元格意味着 A-优先兴趣超过 B-优先兴趣。负单元格意味着相反。匹配利率产生零差异，就像零初始贷款一样。方向遵循配对。在此还款计划下，首先将较高的利率应用于更多的本金。这是一种有条件的计算，而不是关于市场利率将朝哪个方向移动的断言。该工具不允许家庭选择未来的利率路径或锁定仅作为假设显示的利率。实际贷款可能会保持总付款水平、重置后更改付款、每日计算利息、收取费用或将未付利息资本化。这些术语可能会改变主要路径并需要另一种模型。在预算中使用平均利率之前，将利率基础、未偿债务和还款规则记录在一起。这五种观点将这种关系隔离开来，同时将总利息、本金偿还和负担能力作为单独的规划问题。
documents.keywords: The same average rate can produce different interest costs when the loan balance is shrinking Reverse two annual interest-rate blocks on a four-year equal-principal loan, compare the shared debt path and different cash payments, and reconcile why their identical average rate does not imply equal cost.

documents.title: 两个利率指令均包含两年
documents.parentTitle: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 简单平均值是相同的，因为每个汇率恰好出现在四个周期中的两个周期中。利率是假设，而不是报价、概率或预测。平均数不会为每个期间相同金额的债务分配相同的利率。
documents.body: 简单平均值是相同的，因为每个汇率恰好出现在四个周期中的两个周期中。利率是假设，而不是报价、概率或预测。平均数不会为每个期间相同金额的债务分配相同的利率。
documents.keywords: Both rate orders contain two years in each block The simple average is the same because each rate appears for exactly two of the four periods. Rates are assumptions, not quotes, probabilities or forecasts. An equal average does not assign the same rate to the same amount of debt in each period.

documents.title: 固定本金偿还规则使未偿余额相同
documents.parentTitle: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 检查点零是借入的初始金额。每次等额本金偿还之后都会有后续检查点。利息是单独支付的，不会添加到本金中。该图并不意味着实际浮动利率贷款具有这种还款结构；此处固定结构以隔离利率顺序效应。
documents.body: 检查点零是借入的初始金额。每次等额本金偿还之后都会有后续检查点。利息是单独支付的，不会添加到本金中。该图并不意味着实际浮动利率贷款具有这种还款结构；此处固定结构以隔离利率顺序效应。
documents.keywords: The fixed principal-repayment rule makes the outstanding balances identical Checkpoint zero is the initial amount borrowed. Later checkpoints follow each equal principal repayment. Interest is paid separately and never added to principal. The graph does not imply that a real variable-rate loan has this repayment structure; the structure is fixed here to isolate the rate-order effect.

documents.title: 等额本金还款仍然会产生不同的年度现金支付时间表
documents.parentTitle: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 每根金条都包含相同的当年本金偿还额以及来自其自身利率指令的利息。这些是现金流出总额，并非全部借贷成本：本金返还已借的资金。分别将时间表与家庭现金可用性进行比较。
documents.body: 每根金条都包含相同的当年本金偿还额以及来自其自身利率指令的利息。这些是现金流出总额，并非全部借贷成本：本金返还已借的资金。分别将时间表与家庭现金可用性进行比较。
documents.keywords: Equal principal repayments still produce different annual cash-payment schedules Every bar includes the same principal repayment for its year and the interest from its own rate order. These are total cash outflows, not all borrowing cost: principal returns money already borrowed. Compare the schedule with household cash availability separately.

documents.title: 年度利息差异解释了总缺口
documents.parentTitle: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 桥梁每年从A优先案例中减去B优先案例。较高的早期利息可能会超过较低的后期利息，因为更多的本金较早未偿还。委托人可以消除这种差异，因为两种情况在相同日期偿还完全相同的金额。
documents.body: 桥梁每年从A优先案例中减去B优先案例。较高的早期利息可能会超过较低的后期利息，因为更多的本金较早未偿还。委托人可以消除这种差异，因为两种情况在相同日期偿还完全相同的金额。
documents.keywords: Annual interest differences explain the total gap The bridge subtracts the B-first case from the A-first case in each year. Higher early interest can outweigh lower later interest because more principal is outstanding earlier. Principal cancels from this difference because both cases repay exactly the same amounts on the same dates.

documents.title: 更改两个汇率块会改变签名订单效果
documents.parentTitle: 当贷款余额缩减时，相同的平均利率可能会产生不同的利息成本
documents.description: 行替换利率 A，列替换利率 B，保持初始贷款和等本还款日历固定。正单元格意味着将 A 放在第一位会花费更多的利息；负电池意味着成本更低。当利率匹配或没有本金时，就会出现零。单元格是确定性比较，而不是对未来费率路径的估计。
documents.body: 行替换利率 A，列替换利率 B，保持初始贷款和等本还款日历固定。正单元格意味着将 A 放在第一位会花费更多的利息；负电池意味着成本更低。当利率匹配或没有本金时，就会出现零。单元格是确定性比较，而不是对未来费率路径的估计。
documents.keywords: Changing the two rate blocks changes the signed order effect Rows replace rate A and columns replace rate B, holding the initial loan and equal-principal repayment calendar fixed. A positive cell means putting A first costs more interest; a negative cell means it costs less. Zero occurs when rates match or there is no principal. Cells are deterministic comparisons, not estimates of future rate paths.

documents.title: 低收入进入和退出率使用不同的起始群体：阅读背后的人百分比
documents.description: 五张图表将加拿大低收入转型率与其分母、人口数量和配对内流动联系起来，然后构建一个单独的家庭现金缺口示例。
documents.body: 进入率和退出率不能直接相减来得出人员的变化。协调起始人口和流量，然后使用实际家庭资金制定储备计划。加拿大选定的统计数据显示，2022年至2023年间，低收入人群的进入率为4.1%，退出率为34.9%。这些百分比从不同的群体开始。入境对象是最初不属于低收入的纳税人；退出涉及最初收入较低的纳税人。从 34.9 减去 4.1，两个条件利率之间存在 30.8 个百分点的差异。它不衡量总体低收入比例的百分比变化、离开人数减去进入人数或家庭恢复收入的机会。这些图表使用加拿大统计局表 11-10-0024-01，选择加拿大、男女和可变低收入衡量标准。他们保留每个过渡对的第一年和第二年，而不是将观察结果视为单年水平。确定报税者人群和低收入定义 此表的加拿大选择涵盖了这两年报税的 10 个省份中年满 18 岁的报税者。这并不是对每个加拿大居民、儿童或家庭的统计。该衡量标准使用按家庭规模平方根调整的人口普查家庭税后收入，阈值基于调整后收入中位数的一半。每年都会重新估计可变阈值。它与表中 2002 年确定并随后进行价格调整的单独衡量标准不同。图表仅使用变量度量，因此这两个定义永远不会拼接在一起。加拿大统计局的贫困维度中心将这些低收入衡量标准的转变与加拿大基于市场篮子衡量标准的官方贫困衡量标准区分开来。跨越选定的统计阈值本身并不能全面反映一个人的生活成本或财务安全。使用人数来重建两个分母 2022/2023 匹配人口包含 28,303,440 名纳税人。其中，4,439,745 人最初处于低收入状态。初始非低收入组差额为：23,863,695。共有 980,895 名参赛者。将该计数除以 23,863,695 所得结果约为 4.1104%，四舍五入为公布的 4.1%。有 1,549,805 次退出。除以 4,439,745 所得结果约为 34.9075%，四舍五入为 34.9%。因此，较大的退出百分比并不意味着将 34.9% 应用于更大的非低收入群体。分组图表将每个实际转换计数放在其自己的合格起始组旁边。该图中的所有条形都衡量人。保持四种可能的开始到结束状态可见。计数矩阵记录第一年的两种状态和第二年的两种状态。 2022/2023 年，2,889,940 名纳税人仍处于低收入状态，1,549,805 人退出，980,895 人进入，22,882,800 人在这两年中处于低收入之外。将第一行中的两个单元格相加即可重建初始低收入计数。将第一列中的两个单元格相加即可重建后来的低收入计数。添加所有四个单元格即可重建整个匹配的群体。单元格计数和条件率是同一选定对的不同视图。规范化每一行将产生基于行的转换百分比；除以总人口会产生人口份额。该图表显示计数，并明确选择分母。协调变化与以人口为单位衡量的进入者和退出者对内瀑布遵循计数恒等式： 4,439,745 最初低收入 + 980,895 进入者 − 1,549,805 退出 = 第二年 3,870,835 低收入者 。因此，该配对中的低收入人数减少了 568,910 人。如果需要改变匹配人口份额，请将人数变化除以同样的 28,303,440 分母。直接减去公布的进入率和退出率无法执行该计算。桥梁报告了描述性的协调。它没有确定一个人的状况发生变化的原因、将变化归因于一项政策或估计以后的收入中断可能会持续多长时间。这些问题需要额外的证据。相邻过渡对不会创建一个固定面板历史线显示从 2018/2019 年到 2022/2023 年的五对。每对都需要在其两年内提供合格的纳税申报表。参与人群在配对之间可能会发生变化。因此，即使两个标签都指的是 2022 年，2021/2022 年对中的第二年低收入人数不必等于 2022/2023 年对中的第一年计数。在不检查覆盖范围的情况下加入它们将消除两个匹配人口之​​间的差异。文章的源代码检查保留了每对的原始值。它验证所有四个转换单元，包括低收入计数、总匹配计数和四个比率。它不会强迫相邻的对进入一个人为的单一队列，也不会声称相同的人对每个标绘点都有贡献。从自己的现金缺口中建立家庭储备 最终图表提出了一个单独的规划问题。假设基本开支为每月 2,500 加元，可用现金为 2,100 加元，起始准备金为 2,400 加元。选定的缺口是每月400加元。使用该储备金来保持固定的月末差距，一个月后剩余 2,000 加元，三个月后剩余 1,200 加元，六个月后剩余零。第 7 个月，初始储备金未提供的累计金额达到 400 加元。第 12 个月达到 2,400 加元。这些现金数字没有乘以国家进入或退出百分比。更改历史年份会更改源快照；它使家庭场景完好无损。更改支出、收入或准备金会更改现金图表，而无需重写官方观察结果。将统计问题放在财务规划问题旁边统计数据描述了特定纳税人群体中特定收入门槛的变化。现金示例描述了选定的家庭短缺情况。他们可以为规划讨论的不同部分提供信息，同时保留各自的单位和证据。真正的准备金审查还需要支付日期、其他费用、支持资格、保险、储蓄的获得以及使用后重建资金的能力。收入变化可能不规律，年度门槛转变不提供每月收入日历。阅读人口、收入衡量标准和两年参考对。将每个条件百分比与其起始组相匹配。使用人数进行流量调节。检查比较是否遵循相同的匹配群体。使用实际家庭成本和现金日期来构建储备情景。此下载表中最新的一对是
